Make this machine a node of an account on a hub, and see the account's nodes.

A hub keeps an account's nodes, the machines its user logged in from. The daemon keeps a connection to it while logged in, and never waits on it: with the hub down, everything else works as before.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx hub audit verify`](#wdx-hub-audit-verify) | Check that no row of the node's audit chain was changed, removed or inserted |
| [`wdx hub code recover`](#wdx-hub-code-recover) | Set up a new authenticator entry with the recovery key, when the old is lost |
| [`wdx hub code setup`](#wdx-hub-code-setup) | Set up an authenticator entry for this node, and get its recovery key |
| [`wdx hub login`](#wdx-hub-login) | Make this machine a node of your account on a hub |
| [`wdx hub logout`](#wdx-hub-logout) | Leave the hub: this machine is no longer a node of the account |
| [`wdx hub node get`](#wdx-hub-node-get) | Show a node of your account, with its key's fingerprint |
| [`wdx hub node list`](#wdx-hub-node-list) | List the nodes of your account, and which are online |
| [`wdx hub node remove`](#wdx-hub-node-remove) | Remove another node from your account, cutting it off at once |
| [`wdx hub session close`](#wdx-hub-session-close) | Close a session, or every one, either way |
| [`wdx hub session list`](#wdx-hub-session-list) | List the sessions open into this node and from it |
| [`wdx hub session open`](#wdx-hub-session-open) | Open a session into another node of your account, with its code |
| [`wdx hub status`](#wdx-hub-status) | Show this machine's login to a hub and its connection |

## wdx hub audit verify

Check that no row of the node's audit chain was changed, removed or inserted.

```sh
wdx hub audit verify [flags]
```

The daemon walks the chain in order, recomputing each row's hash, and stops at the first that does not match. It works logged out.

### Examples

```sh
# Verify the audit chain
wdx hub audit verify

# As JSON
wdx hub audit verify --json
```

### Output

How many rows the chain has and the last one's hash. With `--json`: {"audit": {"rows": ..., "head": ...}}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`audit_broken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#audit_broken) | 1 | a row of the node's audit chain does not match its hash: the chain was changed |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub code recover

Set up a new authenticator entry with the recovery key, when the old is lost.

```sh
wdx hub code recover [flags]
```

You type the recovery key, hidden as you type it; a wrong one makes the next try wait, from 1 second doubling to 5 minutes. A right one goes on as setup does, with a new recovery key at the end: the old one is spent.

### Examples

```sh
# Recover this node's code
wdx hub code recover
```

### Output

The entry's label and the new recovery key, once. Interactive only: no `--json`.

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `recovered`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`code_not_set_up`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_not_set_up) | 1 | no authenticator code is set up on the node |
| [`code_wrong`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_wrong) | 1 | the code is wrong, used already, or came too soon after a wrong one |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_logged_in) | 1 | this node is not logged in to a hub, or the hub cut it off |
| [`recovery_key_wrong`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#recovery_key_wrong) | 1 | the recovery key is wrong, or came too soon after a wrong one |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub code setup

Set up an authenticator entry for this node, and get its recovery key.

```sh
wdx hub code setup [--replace] [flags]
```

A QR code for your authenticator app is shown, with the secret as text for an app that cannot scan; you type a code from the app back, three tries at most, and get a recovery key, shown once. With a code set up already, `--replace` replaces it, asking first: the old entry stops working, and the sessions open stay. Sessions also need hub.remote\_access on.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--replace` |  | replace the code set up, asking first |

### Examples

```sh
# Set up this node's code
wdx hub code setup

# Replace it with a new entry
wdx hub code setup --replace
```

### Output

The entry's label and the recovery key, once. Interactive only: no `--json`.

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `set_up`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`code_exists`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_exists) | 1 | an authenticator code is set up on this node already |
| [`code_wrong`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_wrong) | 1 | the code is wrong, used already, or came too soon after a wrong one |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_logged_in) | 1 | this node is not logged in to a hub, or the hub cut it off |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub login

Make this machine a node of your account on a hub.

```sh
wdx hub login [--url <url>] [--name <name>] [--no-browser] [flags]
```

Without `--url` the login goes to the central hub, https://wdx-hub.fly.dev; `--url` logs in to a hub of your own instead.

The browser opens on the hub's page, where you log in and approve the machine; the link is printed too, for when none opens. With `--no-browser`, or without a browser to open (wdx deps list), the hub's page and a code to type on it are printed instead, to open in a browser on any device. What to open, and the code, go to stderr, with `--json` too. The login waits until it is approved or denied, at most 10 minutes; Ctrl-C cancels it.

The url is https, or plain http to localhost or 127.0.0.1 only.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <name>` |  | name of this node in the account; the hostname by default |
| `--no-browser` |  | open no browser: print the hub's page and a code to type on it |
| `--url <url>` |  | url of a hub of your own, as https://hub.example.com; the central hub when not given |

### Examples

```sh
# Log in to the central hub, in the browser
wdx hub login

# Log in to a hub of your own
wdx hub login --url https://hub.example.com

# Over SSH, with a code typed on another device
wdx hub login --no-browser

# Name the node, from a script
wdx hub login --name laptop --no-browser --json
```

### Output

The hub's status once logged in. With `--json`: {"result": "logged\_in", "hub": {...}}; the link and code still go to stderr

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `logged_in`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`already_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#already_logged_in) | 1 | this node is logged in to a hub already |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`hub_unreachable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_unreachable) | 3 | the hub cannot be reached, or did not answer as a hub does |
| [`hub_version_unsupported`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_version_unsupported) | 1 | the hub serves no version of the API this wdx speaks |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`login_cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#login_cancelled) | 1 | the login was cancelled, or another replaced it |
| [`login_denied`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#login_denied) | 1 | the login was denied on the hub, or the account is disabled |
| [`login_expired`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#login_expired) | 1 | the login was not approved in time |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub logout

Leave the hub: this machine is no longer a node of the account.

```sh
wdx hub logout [flags]
```

The hub is asked to revoke this node, then the node's key, certificate and login are deleted here, whether the hub heard or not: without its key, the node is of no use to anyone. Projects, agents and docs stay.

### Examples

```sh
# Leave the hub
wdx hub logout

# From a script
wdx hub logout --json
```

### Output

That it left, and whether the hub heard. With `--json`: {"result": "logged\_out", "hub\_told": true|false, "hub": {...}}, the hub as it was

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `logged_out`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_logged_in) | 1 | this node is not logged in to a hub, or the hub cut it off |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub node get

Show a node of your account, with its key's fingerprint.

```sh
wdx hub node get (--id <id> | --name <name>) [flags]
```

Show a node of your account, with its key's fingerprint

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the node |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the node (case-insensitive) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`

### Examples

```sh
# A node by name
wdx hub node get --name laptop

# By id, as JSON
wdx hub node get --id node-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The node. With `--json`: {"node": {...}}

### Errors

## wdx hub node remove

Remove another node from your account, cutting it off at once.

```sh
wdx hub node remove (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--yes] [flags]
```

The hub closes its connection and renews no certificate for it. You are asked first; `--yes` answers in advance, and with `--json`, or without a terminal, it is required. This machine cannot remove itself: wdx hub logout does.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the node |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the node (case-insensitive) |
| `--yes` |  | remove it without asking |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- with `--json`: one of `--yes`

### Examples

```sh
# Remove a lost laptop
wdx hub node remove --name laptop

# From a script
wdx hub node remove --id node-1a2b3c4d --yes --json
```

### Output

The removed node, as it was. With `--json`: {"result": "removed", "node": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `removed`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`hub_unreachable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_unreachable) | 3 | the hub cannot be reached, or did not answer as a hub does |
| [`hub_version_unsupported`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_version_unsupported) | 1 | the hub serves no version of the API this wdx speaks |
| [`node_is_this`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_is_this) | 1 | the node is this one: leaving is wdx hub logout |
| [`node_not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_not_found) | 1 | the account has no node of this name or id |
| [`not_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_logged_in) | 1 | this node is not logged in to a hub, or the hub cut it off |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub session close

Close a session, or every one, either way.

```sh
wdx hub session close (--id <id> | --all) [flags]
```

Closing an outgoing session ends this node's access, telling the host when it can; closing an incoming one cuts off whoever is connected from that node, which finds out at its next use.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | close every session open, both ways |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the session |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--all`

### Examples

```sh
# Close one session
wdx hub session close --id sess-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

# Close every one, from a script
wdx hub session close --all --json
```

### Output

The sessions closed, as they were. With `--json`: {"result": "closed", "session": {...}}, or "sessions": [...] with `--all`

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `closed`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`session_not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#session_not_found) | 1 | no session of this id is open |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub session open

Open a session into another node of your account, with its code.

```sh
wdx hub session open --node <name> [--code <code>] [flags]
```

The code is the one your authenticator app shows for that node (wdx hub code setup there); without `--code` it is asked for, and `--json` needs it. A code opens one session, and is never logged. After a wrong code, the next try waits, from 1 second doubling to 5 minutes. With a session into the node open already, nothing is asked.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--code <code>` |  | the node's authenticator code now; asked for when not given |
| `--node <name>` |  | name of the node to open a session into |

- `--node` is required
- with `--json`: one of `--code`

### Examples

```sh
# Open a session into the desktop, typing its code
wdx hub session open --node desktop

# From a script
wdx hub session open --node desktop --code 492817 --json
```

### Output

The session. With `--json`: {"result": "opened", "session": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `opened` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`code_not_set_up`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_not_set_up) | 1 | no authenticator code is set up on the node |
| [`code_wrong`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#code_wrong) | 1 | the code is wrong, used already, or came too soon after a wrong one |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`hub_unreachable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_unreachable) | 3 | the hub cannot be reached, or did not answer as a hub does |
| [`hub_version_unsupported`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#hub_version_unsupported) | 1 | the hub serves no version of the API this wdx speaks |
| [`node_key_mismatch`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_key_mismatch) | 1 | the node showed a key other than the one pinned for it in an earlier session |
| [`node_not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_not_found) | 1 | the account has no node of this name or id |
| [`node_offline`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_offline) | 1 | the node is not connected to the hub, or did not answer in time |
| [`node_version_unsupported`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#node_version_unsupported) | 1 | the two nodes speak no version in common between them: update the older |
| [`not_logged_in`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_logged_in) | 1 | this node is not logged in to a hub, or the hub cut it off |
| [`remote_access_off`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#remote_access_off) | 1 | the node allows no sessions: hub.remote\_access is off there |
| [`too_many_streams`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#too_many_streams) | 1 | the account has as many streams open through the hub as it may |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx hub status

Show this machine's login to a hub and its connection.

```sh
wdx hub status [flags]
```

The connection is connected, connecting, offline (lost, and tried again), logged\_out, revoked (another node removed this one) or disabled (the hub's admin disabled the account). Not being logged in is a state, not an error.

### Examples

```sh
# Whether this machine is connected
wdx hub status

# As JSON
wdx hub status --json
```

### Output

The state on the first line, then what to do about it. With `--json`: {"hub": {...}}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
